Subject: MSA redlines: Section 7.2 (latency SLO) + Exhibit G rollback

Hi Aiden / Dexus legal team,

Thanks again for the productive call yesterday. Per our commercial review, Dexus submitted MSA redlines that touch two items we need to resolve before procurement can route:

1) Section 7.2 — Dexus wants a hard latency SLO metric tied to a service credit table. We have an internally approved tolerance band but cannot accept the proposed credit ladder as-is (it exposes unlimited downside for burst pools).

2) Exhibit G — Dexus proposed a rollback right that would allow reclassification of nodes post-implementation. That conflicts with our ordering and billing exhibits. We can offer a gated rollback (time-limited, capped reclassification) but need legal to align language.

I've attached their redlines and a suggested Exhibit G substitution that narrows the rollback window. Karthik and Mina, can you review the attached and advise which pieces are non-starters and which we can compromise on (e.g., latency SLO anchored to median p95 with a maximum credit cap)?

Aiden / Samira: if you can call out the absolute must-haves from Dexus (e.g., regulator-driven SLA need), that will help prioritize tradeoffs. We want to avoid extensive rework in procurement.

Next steps I propose:
- Redwood legal (Karthik/Mina) to provide a redline back by EOD tomorrow (Fri 6/13).
- If Dexus can accept a capped credit schedule and a 30-day limited rollback, we can proceed to DocuSign and procurement sign-off.

Thanks,

Vanessa Ortiz

Vanessa —

Appreciate the note and the proposed Exhibit G. Aiden and I reviewed with our compliance team; the latency SLO is a regulatory ask for one of our customers (real-time fraud detection). The current credit ladder exists to provide teeth in the event of repeated regressions — removing it entirely isn't possible for us.

That said, we are open to negotiating caps and a shorter rollback window. Are you able to share Redwood's proposal for a capped credit table (max aggregate credit per quarter) rather than a percentage-based unlimited credit? If we can limit exposure, legal may be able to accept.

We uploaded our tracked redlines here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcDeFg (Dexus_MSA_redlines.docx).

Vanessa / team —

Thanks for the heads-up and the draft exhibit. Quick read-through notes:

- Section 7.2: We cannot accept an unbounded service credit ladder tied to p100 without an explicit cap. Proposed wording: "Redwood's aggregate service credit liability shall not exceed 25% of the quarterly invoice for the impacted service in any rolling 90-day period." This gives Dexus a remedy while protecting Redwood's commercial exposure.

- SLO definition: Recommend anchoring to p95 measured on production traffic for the applicable model endpoint and exclude scheduled maintenance windows and authenticated DoS incidents.

- Exhibit G rollback: We can offer a 30-day rollback window post-cutover limited to one reclassification event per annual term and limited to nodes representing up to 15% of the original committed capacity. That should bridge the gap with Dexus while keeping our implementation guarantees intact.

I'll prepare a tracked redline back and upload it to the shared Drive by EOD tomorrow. Jonas — please pull the projected invoice math for a 25% cap and an example quarter so we can show impact to Dexus' procurement. Mina — flag any other commercial terms that need escalation.

Karthik
Sr. Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference

Thanks Karthik — that cap proposal looks reasonable to us as a starting point. Our procurement team did ask for one addition: if Redwood's cap applies, can you add a clause that allows an emergency escalator (one-off exception) where, with executive sign-off from both parties, an additional remedial credit may be applied for a severe outage (defined as >72 continuous minutes impacting p95 across >60% of production endpoints)?

We understand this is an exceptional carve-out and are happy to document the executive sign-off path and attach it as an annex instead of embedding as a standing right. That would preserve Redwood's predictability while giving our legal/compliance a path for very severe incidents.

If Redwood can accept that formulation, we can move to a clean DocuSign route next week.

Aiden
Head of Platform Partnerships | Dexus AI
